questions.prompt: An external client's valid Blob SAS fails after the storage firewall is restricted to selected networks. Its IP is not allowed. What addresses the network problem without broadening SAS permissions?

options.text: Allow the client's approved public egress IP in the storage firewall.
options.explanation: The request needs an allowed network path as well as valid authorization.

options.text: Add write permission to the SAS.
options.explanation: More data permissions do not override the firewall.

options.text: Replace the SAS with the storage account key.
options.explanation: A key does not exempt this client from network filtering.

options.text: Extend the SAS expiry by a week.
options.explanation: The token is already valid; duration is not the failing condition.

questions.prompt: A storage account has an approved subnet rule, but defaultAction is Allow. Other internet clients with valid authorization can still read blobs. Which change enforces the selected-network allowlist?

options.explanation: Unmatched public-endpoint traffic is then denied.

options.text: Assign the approved subnet Azure Reader.
options.explanation: Subnets do not gain data-plane network exclusivity through Reader.
TLS policy does not enforce a subnet allowlist.

options.text: Switch the account from LRS to ZRS.
options.explanation: Redundancy is unrelated to client network admission.

questions.prompt: A VM subnet must access Blob Storage through a service endpoint while the storage firewall defaults to Deny. Which two configurations are required for this network path?

options.text: Enable the appropriate Storage service endpoint on the subnet.
options.explanation: The endpoint supplies the subnet identity and service route.

options.text: Add that subnet to the storage account's virtual network rules.
options.explanation: The account must explicitly allow the subnet.

options.text: Create a Blob private endpoint as well.
options.explanation: Private Link is an alternative path, not a requirement for this service-endpoint design.
Network connectivity does not require removing data authorization.

questions.prompt: A user can view a storage account's ARM properties but cannot download blobs from an unlisted network. What explains this difference?

options.text: Storage firewall rules govern data-plane requests, while ARM management has separate authorization.
options.explanation: Viewing resource configuration does not prove blob network reachability.

options.text: Viewing ARM properties automatically grants blob read access.
options.explanation: Management visibility does not provide data authorization or bypass filtering.

options.text: Only Archive blobs are subject to the firewall.
options.explanation: The firewall is not restricted to one access tier.

options.text: Every portal visit automatically issues a firewall-bypassing SAS.
options.explanation: Portal use does not establish a universal network bypass.
